unit: EPA_points (PLL points above league-average expected opportunity outcome)
numerator_definition: closed-form sd of the value components under chance alone at the player's own opportunity counts
formula: sqrt of the sum of component null variances; two-point terms carry a factor of 4 because a two-point attempt pays 2 points
interpretation: How far from zero luck alone could put this player, given how many opportunities he had.
known_limitations: Assumes opportunity outcomes are INDEPENDENT, which shots within a game are not exactly. NULL, not 0, where the player had no opportunities of a class -- reporting 0 would say the value is known exactly. No resampling is used because none is needed: a bootstrap over the same 80 shot outcomes estimates the same binomial variance with Monte Carlo noise added.

denominator_definition: the chance sd at the player's own opportunity volume
interpretation: How far a season is from what luck alone could produce. THE ONLY VALUE-ADJACENT MEASURE IN THIS PROJECT THAT IS CROSS-POSITION COMPARABLE, because it does not depend on a peer group's size or composition.
cross_position_comparable: A: same meaning in every role
known_limitations: IT IS STILL NOT A VALUE MEASURE. A goalie's +2 and an attackman's +2 mean equally UNUSUAL seasons, not equal contributions. Using it as an award input would rank unusualness.

denominator_definition: the chance sd of faceoff value at the player's own draw count
interpretation: Whether a faceoff season is distinguishable from chance.
known_limitations: League sd 1.830, implying a skill share of variance of 0.70 -- the strongest in the framework. The MEAN across all 47 draw-takers is -1.01: non-specialists who take occasional draws lose them at a clearly below-average rate, and the specialists' surplus is largely funded by wing players taking draws when the specialist is off the field.

denominator_definition: the chance sd of goalie value at the player's own shots faced
interpretation: Whether a goalie season is distinguishable from chance. THE RIGHT COLUMN FOR COMPARING GOALIES TO NON-GOALIES, where raw goalie value is not.
known_limitations: League sd 1.320, skill share 0.43.

denominator_definition: the chance sd of shooting value at the player's own attempt mix
interpretation: Whether a shooting season is distinguishable from chance.
known_limitations: The league sd of this column is 1.067 against 1.0 under the pure-chance null, implying only about 12% of the observed between-player variance in shooting value is skill.

display_name: MVP / Statistical Tewaaraton / composite player score
numerator_definition: weighted combination of value components across positions
interpretation: TEMPTING BECAUSE every component is in the same unit and a weighted sum is one line of SQL.
known_limitations: NO COMPOSITE, AWARD SCORE, WAR, REPLACEMENT LEVEL OR CROSS-POSITION RANKING EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY, and Phase 8 adds an automated test that fails if one appears. THE UNIT IS SHARED; THE SCALE IS NOT. Opportunity bases differ by 6.6x in observed spread, the only class-A value-adjacent metric measures unusualness rather than contribution, and positional percentiles remove the group effect without creating comparability of value. A cross-position weighting is a JUDGEMENT that has to be argued for in the open; no metric in this system supplies one. Category leaders and within-role rankings ARE published.

denominator_definition: sum of the absolute values of all components
interpretation: How much of a player's MEASURED value is the one defensive act the feed counts. Mean share among faceoff specialists: 0.05.
known_limitations: A LOW SHARE FOR A DEFENDER IS A MEASUREMENT STATEMENT, NOT A PERFORMANCE ONE. PARTIAL by construction. It measures caused turnovers above the position group's per-game average and NOTHING ELSE. Off-ball defence, help positioning, matchup difficulty, forcing a bad shot instead of a turnover, shot suppression, sliding, recovery and communication leave no trace in this feed. A value of 0.0 does NOT mean 'an average defender'. The denominator is games played, because the feed has no minutes, shifts or lineups.

denominator_definition: sum of the absolute values of all components
interpretation: Where a player's measured value comes from. Denominated in ABSOLUTE magnitudes because the components are signed residuals: a share of a signed sum can be negative or unbounded and is not interpretable.
known_limitations: ACROSS THE 13 SPECIALISTS THE FACEOFF SHARE AVERAGES 0.53 AND SPANS 0.12-0.88 -- so 'a FOGO's value is his faceoffs' is true on average and emphatically not true player by player. Petey LaSalla's measured value is 87% offensive. Read faceoff_value_raw directly rather than inferring it from a total.

denominator_definition: sum of the absolute values of all components
interpretation: The offensive share of measured value.
known_limitations: See faceoff_share_of_absolute_value.

interpretation: Penalties committed. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY -- there is no penalty component in the value framework, though the event coefficient (-0.417) is estimated and published.

Splitting credit between shooter and assister is a DEFENSIBLE alternative, but it changes what shooting_value means, so the choice belongs to the phase that needs it rather than being slipped in as a default. Publishing an 'adjusted' number less reliable than the unadjusted one would be a regression. Pooling seasons does not help: a 2022 roster and a 2026 roster are not the same unit, so extra seasons replicate the question rather than adding connectivity. known_limitations: PLL's man-up tag lands on GOALS ONLY -- all 90 tagged events in 2026 are valid goals -- so man-up shot volume must come from the official box score and no man-up POSSESSION exists. The denominator is the extra-man opportunity, never a possession. No penalty-clock state is reconstructed. The tagged goal count matches official powerPlayGoals in 97 of 100 team-games; the residual is exposed as man_up_goals_pbp_minus_official.

known_limitations: PLL's man-up tag lands on GOALS ONLY -- all 90 tagged events in 2026 are valid goals -- so man-up shot volume must come from the official box score and no man-up POSSESSION exists. The denominator is the extra-man opportunity, never a possession. No penalty-clock state is reconstructed.

interpretation: TEMPTING BECAUSE possessions.has_man_up_shot exists and looks like a man-up flag.
known_limitations: IT IS A GOAL FLAG. It is TRUE for exactly 90 possessions and every one contains a man-up goal, so the column would be a renamed goal count and every rate on it is degenerate -- man-up shooting percentage computed that way is 1.000 for all 8 teams. Penalty events carry no possession linkage either, so man-up possessions cannot be recovered from penalty timing without inventing the state. A regression test asserts the goals-only property, so if PLL starts tagging missed man-up shots this decision gets revisited rather than silently inherited. MISSING INPUT: man-up tagging on shot events, or penalty-to-possession linkage.

interpretation: Draws lost.

interpretation: The most reliably measured team rate in this system: 2,618 league draws, and the analogous player rate is the only one with strong individual identification.

interpretation: Draws won.
known_limitations: Official chosen over play-by-play: the two agree in 99 of 100 team-games and the official denominator is the cleaner one.

interpretation: Draw volume. The official denominator includes NO-DECISION draws (violations and redraws), which is why faceoffsWon + faceoffsLost falls 1-2 short of faceoffs in 8 games.
known_limitations: Using wins+losses as the denominator instead would silently drop the no-decision draws and inflate every win percentage.

interpretation: Loose-ball recoveries.
known_limitations: Official box-score numerator. 16 games carry unresolved ground-ball residuals from Phase 4.25.

interpretation: Recovery rate. The denominator is BOTH sides of the ball, because ground balls are recovered on both -- dividing by offensive possessions alone would misattribute the rate.
known_limitations: Official box-score numerator. 16 games carry unresolved ground-ball residuals from Phase 4.25. No offensive-ground-ball or contested-ground-ball percentage is computed: the feed supplies no such denominator.

interpretation: Game pace including the opponent's share.

interpretation: The denominator of every defensive efficiency metric. Sums league-wide to exactly the same total as offensive possessions.
known_limitations: See offensive_possessions.

interpretation: Share of a team's offence that began on a won draw. The one possession-source split the feed supports.
known_limitations: The complementary splits are NOT published: 922 possessions carry start_reason='other_confirmed_control' (team known, mechanism unknown), so a defensive-stop vs. ground-ball split would assign ~21% of possessions to a bucket the feed never established.

numerator_definition: offensive possessions whose start_reason is faceoff_win
interpretation: How many possessions arrived off the draw.
known_limitations: Faceoff-started possessions are never flagged ambiguous (1,326/1,326 faceoff team attributions resolved), so this split is trustworthy where the fuller possession-source split is not.

numerator_definition: reconstructed possessions with this team on offence
interpretation: The denominator of every offensive efficiency metric.

interpretation: How many more times a team had the ball than its opponents did. Driven almost entirely by the faceoff, which is why it tracks faceoff_win_pct closely.
known_limitations: Small by construction and heavily faceoff-driven; it is not an independent skill from faceoff win percentage. Sums to 0 league-wide.

numerator_definition: points on possessions of a given start type
interpretation: TEMPTING BECAUSE Lacrosse Reference publishes efficiency by possession source and the possession layer has a start_reason column.

ONLY THE FACEOFF SPLIT IS PUBLISHED, because faceoff-started possessions are never ambiguous. MISSING INPUT: a possession-start mechanism in the feed.

interpretation: PACE, expressed in possession COUNTS. Deliberately not in seconds: possession counts are structurally validated, possession durations are not a valid time measure.
known_limitations: Higher is neither good nor bad -- it is a style. A possession SPAN is the interval from a possession's first logged event to its last. It is NOT time of possession: it recovers a median 75% of PLL's official figure with a 0.54-1.00 range and r=0.58, because it excludes transition, clearing and dead-ball time. Use the official figure.

interpretation: Total possessions the team was involved in. The correct denominator for two-sided rates such as ground balls.
known_limitations: Not a pace measure on its own -- divide by games.

interpretation: GOALS, not points. A two-point goal counts once here.

interpretation: Finishing rate against the keeper, net of misses. The offensive mirror of save_pct_vs_shots_on_goal.

interpretation: PLL points from the shooting table. Identical to points_scored, derived from a different table, and asserted equal on every row.
known_limitations: Kept as an independent cross-check on the possession-derived total, not as a second answer.

interpretation: The PLL-native shooting metric: it is the only one that credits two-point volume. League 2026: 0.290.
known_limitations: Diverges from shooting_pct exactly to the extent a team scores two-point goals. That divergence is the point of the metric, not a defect.

interpretation: Finishing accuracy. DELIBERATELY NOT points per shot: a team that scores two two-point goals on two shots shot 100%, not 200%.

interpretation: Attempt volume.

interpretation: Goals conceded (not points).
known_limitations: GOALS, not points: a two-point goal against counts once here and twice in points_allowed.

interpretation: The defensive mirror of shooting_pct.

interpretation: THE authoritative time-of-possession column. No reconstructed alternative is published anywhere in this project.
known_limitations: Official and unverifiable against the event log -- the log has no comparable quantity. A possession SPAN is the interval from a possession's first logged event to its last. It is NOT time of possession: it recovers a median 75% of PLL's official figure with a 0.54-1.00 range and r=0.58, because it excludes transition, clearing and dead-ball time. Use the official figure.

interpretation: Per-game official ToP.
known_limitations: See time_of_possession_official_seconds.

interpretation: TEMPTING BECAUSE the possession layer has a duration on every row and summing it looks like time of possession.
known_limitations: IT IS NOT TIME OF POSSESSION. The span from a possession's first logged event to its last excludes the interval between the previous possession's last logged event and this one's first -- transition, the clear, the dead ball. Median coverage of PLL's official figure is 0.751 with a 0.536-0.998 range and r = 0.58, and mean absolute error in team possession SHARE is 4.9 percentage points. A 25% shortfall that varied consistently would be rescalable; a 0.54-1.00 range at r=0.58 is not. MISSING INPUT: an event stream that logs possession start as well as possession action. NOTE the clock itself is sound -- three independent checks confirm it -- so this is a coverage problem, not a timing problem, which is why possession-LENGTH splits remain defensible.

interpretation: The one countable defensive act in this feed. 741 league-wide.

interpretation: The expected return on a long shot, in the same units as points_per_one_point_attempt. League 2026: 0.269 against 0.293.

The league-level gap of -0.024 is INSIDE one standard error of the two-point return (0.030), so 2026 does not establish that the long shot returns less -- only that it does not clearly return more.

interpretation: Long-range volume. 536 league-wide in 2026.

interpretation: Long-range accuracy. League 2026: 13.4%.
